output_json.patch_notes: Added a check at the top of FileResourceManager.getResource(String p) (right after the leading-slash strip) that returns null immediately if the resulting path contains a backslash character. This is a root-cause fix at the shared filesystem-resolution sink used by every trace in the alert. Also added core/src/test/java/io/undertow/server/handlers/resource/FileResourceManagerTest.java with: (1) a sanity test that normal resource retrieval still works, (2) tests asserting several backslash-based traversal path variants return null, and (3) a test that proves the guard is unconditional (not merely relying on the current platform's File separator semantics) by creating a real file whose literal name contains a backslash and asserting it is still never resolved -- this test was verified to FAIL on the pre-fix code (returns a non-null FileResource) and PASS after the fix, confirming it's a genuine regression witness even though the underlying vulnerability's most severe manifestation (backslash treated as a directory separator) is Windows-specific and can't be reproduced via real filesystem behavior on the Linux CI container.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavioral change: resource paths containing a literal backslash character are now always rejected (404/null resource), even on Unix-like systems where backslash is historically a legal filename character and even outside traversal contexts. This is an intentional, standard mitigation (matching how other servlet containers treat raw backslash in HTTP paths) since legitimate URIs are '/'-delimited and should never contain a raw backslash; any real-world impact is limited to resources whose filenames literally contain '\', which is highly unusual. No other behavior of FileResourceManager, CanonicalPathUtils, DefaultServlet, or ServletContextImpl was changed. Full core+servlet package build and the targeted existing test suites (FileHandlerTestCase, FileHandlerIndexTestCase, FileErrorPageHandlerTestCase, ContentEncodedResourceTestCase, RealPathTestCase, GetResourceTestCase) all pass unmodified against the patched code.
output_json.summary: Fixed a Windows-specific CWE-022 path traversal in FileResourceManager.getResource(), the common sink for all four traces in the alert (direct FileResourceManager calls, ServletContextImpl.getRealPath -> CanonicalPathUtils.canonicalize, and DefaultServlet.getPath/doGet). Upstream request-path handling (CanonicalPathUtils, DefaultServlet#isAllowed) only recognizes '/' as a path separator, but java.io.File on Windows also treats '\' as a separator. An attacker-supplied path containing backslash sequences (e.g. '..\..\secret.txt') would pass the '/'-based traversal checks unchanged and then be resolved by `new File(base, path)` using Windows' backslash-aware File system, escaping the configured resource base directory. The fix adds a single guard in getResource(): any resource path containing a literal backslash is rejected (returns null) before it ever reaches `new File(base, path)`, regardless of the OS the server actually runs on. This closes the root cause for every caller that funnels through this sink, including same-class bypass variants (any position/count of backslashes, mixed with '..' segments, leading backslash, etc.), since the check is unconditional rather than tied to one specific traversal pattern.
